episodes.164182: A low pressure formed in the Gulf of Mexico along with a cold front. These two features pushed across the state as it started to deepen. This caused high winds and spawned a tornado in West Central Florida.
episodes.164211: A low pressure formed in the Gulf of Mexico along with a cold front. These two features pushed across the state as it started to deepen. This caused high marine wind gust.
episodes.164384: An upper trough northeast of the Aloha State caused enough instability to produce showers and isolated thunderstorms over leeward portions of the Big Island of Hawaii.  The precipitation resulted in small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.164725: Heavy rain fell across parts of northwest Oregon along with minor river flooding. The heaviest rain fell along and just north of a front that held nearly stationary from Newport to Albany to Mount Jefferson.
episodes.164940: A strong low pressure system over the Gulf of Mexico and attendant cold front moved across South FL, bringing severe storms with it. A Tornado Watch was issued during the early morning hours. An unstable atmosphere and plentiful moisture preceded the front, and strong winds aloft aided in the development of thunderstorms with strong wind gusts across the Biscayne Bay and Atlantic waters.
episodes.164941: A strong low pressure system over the Gulf of Mexico and attendant cold front moved across South FL, bringing severe storms with it. A Tornado Watch was issued during the early morning hours. An unstable atmosphere and plentiful moisture preceded the front, and strong winds aloft aided in the development of thunderstorms with strong wind gusts across portions of Miami-Dade County.
episodes.164992: Minor flooding occurred along the White River. Low-lying fields and woodlands were flooded, along with a few river access roads. Widespread rain increased the night of the 17th into early on the 18th as a mid level shortwave trough pushed southeastward into the Plains states and interacted with a warm front lifting northward across the Ohio River Valley. A southwesterly 850 mb low level jet ramped up to 40 to 45 knots, and precipitable water values were very high for this time of year. An additional one to two inches of rain fell, pushing the river just above flood stage.
episodes.165186: A stalled front was in place across the area from Dec 17-18 acting as the focus for widespread rainfall. Initially the heavy rain threat was across northern Arkansas and southern Missouri but by the 18th, rain expanded south. A few of our rivers were affected and rose above flood stage.
episodes.165359: A small, intense low presure system moving onshore southwest mainland Florida and attended low pressure trough extending to the southwest produced a squall line and brief episode of gale-force convective wind gusts across the Florida Keys.
